reason: This narrative (2 Kings 18-19) demonstrates the opposite principle. The text shows the Assyrian elite (King Sennacherib, the Rabshakeh, and military officials) boasting of their superiority and power, yet they are ultimately defeated by God's intervention. The regular people of Jerusalem are saved not through elite status or military might, but through their king's humble prayer and trust in God. The narrative explicitly undermines elite self-confidence by showing that 185,000 soldiers are slain overnight by God's angel, rendering the boasted military superiority irrelevant. The text emphasizes God's sovereignty over all rulers and nations, suggesting that moral and spiritual trust matters more than elite status.
